parts.visual:
Every 90 days, the CEO puts on a clean shirt, prints out a 50-page presentation, and sits in a room with their investors for four hours. The CEO shows them exactly how much money was burned, how many users quit, and why the new feature failed. The investors ask brutal, uncomfortable questions.

The Ritual:
1. The Board Meeting: A formal, legally required meeting where the CEO reports the exact financial and strategic health of the company to the Board.
2. The Rule of No Surprises: The worst thing a CEO can do is surprise the board with bad news *during* the meeting. Good CEOs call board members individually a week before the meeting to warn them about disasters.
parts.audio: A board meeting is not a marketing pitch. It is an operational autopsy. If you go into a board meeting and tell your VCs that everything is perfect, they will instantly know you are either lying or completely blind to the reality of your own business.

questions.question: A CEO sends the 'Board Deck' (the 50-page presentation) to the investors 10 minutes before the board meeting starts. Why is this a massive mistake?
options: The file might be too big.

It wastes the entire meeting. If the investors haven't read the deck, the CEO has to spend 3 hours just reading the slides out loud. The deck should be sent 48 hours in advance so the investors can read it, and the meeting can be used purely for high-level strategic debate.
The investors don't know how to open PDFs.
questions.correct_answer: It wastes the entire meeting. If the investors haven't read the deck, the CEO has to spend 3 hours just reading the slides out loud. The deck should be sent 48 hours in advance so the investors can read it, and the meeting can be used purely for high-level strategic debate.
questions.explanation: Board meetings are for discussion, not reading practice.

questions.question: Listen to the VC complaining about a bad board meeting. What did the CEO fail to do?
questions.tts_text: The CEO talked for three straight hours about how great the new logo looks. They completely ignored the fact that we have 4 months of runway left and our main competitor just stole our biggest client. They were hiding from the real problems.
options: Avoiding the Red Flags. Elite CEOs spend 10% of the board meeting on the good news, and 90% aggressively discussing the terrifying threats that might kill the company. The board is there to help solve existential crises, not to applaud the logo.
questions.correct_answer: Avoiding the Red Flags. Elite CEOs spend 10% of the board meeting on the good news, and 90% aggressively discussing the terrifying threats that might kill the company. The board is there to help solve existential crises, not to applaud the logo.
questions.explanation: Use the board's brainpower to solve your worst nightmares.

questions.question: What are 'Board Minutes'?
options: The 60 seconds before the meeting starts.

The formal, legally binding written record of exactly what was discussed and voted on during the meeting. If the company is sued or acquired 5 years later, lawyers will read these minutes to prove the board acted legally and responsibly.
questions.correct_answer: The formal, legally binding written record of exactly what was discussed and voted on during the meeting. If the company is sued or acquired 5 years later, lawyers will read these minutes to prove the board acted legally and responsibly.
questions.explanation: If it is not in the minutes, legally, it never happened.

questions.question: At the end of the meeting, the board asks the CEO and all employees to leave the room. The board members stay inside alone. What is this called?
options: The Closed Session (or Executive Session). This is a standard governance practice where the independent board members and VCs talk privately without management present. They use this time to evaluate the CEO's personal performance and discuss the CEO's salary.
questions.correct_answer: The Closed Session (or Executive Session). This is a standard governance practice where the independent board members and VCs talk privately without management present. They use this time to evaluate the CEO's personal performance and discuss the CEO's salary.
questions.explanation: The only time the bosses talk without the employee in the room.

questions.question: Order the words to describe the golden rule of board management:
questions.explanation: Bad news should be delivered via a private phone call before the meeting.
